2026 Outlook
• Thailand palm supply 
recovered, pressuring early-
quarter CPO prices.
• Policy support (B7/B20 from

quarter domestic demand.
• Export environment stayed 
active, while Thailand 
introduced CPO export permit 
control effective 7 April 2026.
• Core operating income 
remained resilient, supported 
by stable throughput and export 
execution.
• Revenue and margins were 
impacted by lower CPO selling 
prices.
• Product mix discipline and 
channel balancing helped 
contain downside pressure.
• Tight inventory-cost 
management and flexible 
channel allocation across food, 
energy, and export.
• Accelerate value-added mix 
and readiness of strategic 
projects (Crushing Mill Phase 3, 
Refinery and Dry-Fractionation).
• Keep executing Jump+ 
roadmap to strengthen 
earnings quality into 2027.
• Stabilize margin quality: tighten 
inventory turns, pricing 
discipline, and cost control 
Upgrade earnings mix: increase 
value-added products and 
improve contribution from 
downstream channels.
• Protect growth optionality: 
secure feedstock, keep export 
flexibility, and actively manage 
policy/FX volatility.
“Against a volatile palm oil cycle, PCE is 
converting integrated scale into earnings 
quality by tightening execution, 
accelerating value-added growth, and 
advancing Jump+ milestones toward a 
stronger 2027.”

1Q26 PALM OIL INDUSTRY : IMPACTING FACTOR TO FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
PCE Drives a fully-integrated palm oil business to achieve sustainable growth and excellence
• CPO price: In Q1/2026, the average crude palm oil price 
stood at THB 33,774/ton, increasing slightly by 0.33% 
YoY.
• Soybean oil price: The average soybean oil price rose 
sharply by 23.73% YoY to THB 40,729/ton, driven by 
higher demand from the U.S. biofuel industry and China’s 
soybean demand.
• Price spread: The average price spread between 
soybean oil and crude palm oil widened to THB 6,954/ton.
• Key factor in March 2026: Rising crude oil prices, driven 
by the Middle East conflict, supported higher crude palm 
oil prices as palm oil is also used as an alternative energy 
source.
Global Market Dynamics 1Q26
CPO prices are likely to remain volatile, supported 
by crude oil trends and biofuel demand, while the 
wider spread with soybean oil may continue to 
pressure market margins.

1)
Gross Profit in 1Q26 was THB 223.3 million, up 
80.4% YoY, with GPM improving to 4.3% from 2.3% 
YoY and 3.5% QoQ. The YoY improvement was 
driven by better cost management and a more 
favorable product mix, particularly downstream 
products, while the QoQ decline reflected softer 
revenue and continued palm oil price volatility.
2) EBITDA & EBITDA Margin FY25:  EBITDA decreased 
from THB 75.2 million in 1Q25 to THB 63.6 million in 
1Q26, while adjusted EBITDA margin decreased from 
THB 162.6 million to THB 156.6 million. Adjusted 
EBITDA margin slightly increase from 3.1% to 3.2%.
3) Net Profit & NPM FY25: Net profit declined to THB 6.7 
million in 1Q26, down 76.1% YoY, with NPM decreasing 
to 0.1% from 0.5%, mainly due to the 104.8 million loss 
from changes in the fair value of derivative instruments. 
This temporary recognition timing effect pressuring net 
performance during the period.

•
In 1Q26, PCE’s total sales volume increased to 129,194 
tons, up from 108,633 tons in 1Q25, reflecting solid growth 
across key product categories, mainly driven by higher 
CPO and refined product sales. 
•
CPO continued to be the main contributor to sales 
volume, driven by improved palm output and market 
demand, while B100 and RINTIP are expected to play a 
greater role in supporting PCE’s growth this year.
•
Government export controls and higher biodiesel 
blending could increase domestic CPO demand, 
potentially limiting Thailand’s CPO exports as supply is 
balanced across food, energy, and export markets.
PCE delivered solid sales volume growth in 1Q26, supported by 
higher CPO sales and a strong rebound in exports, while 
maintaining a solid domestic market base.
